5 Overtaking
5.8 Situations when you must not overtake  
Specifically, it is prohibited to overtake:
In any place or circumstance where visibility is not sufficient to be able to complete the manoeuvre or abort it once started, unless the two directions of traffic are clearly marked out and the manoeuvre can be completed without moving into the zone reserved for the opposite direction, specifically:
- On bends and changes in gradient with reduced visibility.
- When the weather conditions significantly reduce visibility (fog, heavy rain or when the sun is low, dazzling drivers). In these circumstances, you should never overtake.
- Behind a vehicle which is also overtaking if, due to its size or other features, it prevents the vehicle’s driver from seeing the road ahead.
(Página 191 del manual 'Learning to drive')

(Página 193 del manual 'Learning to drive')

In a two way roadway, where there are three lanes, separated by broken (discontinuous) longitudinal centre lines, a driver intending to turn to the left, must be positioned in the centre lane.

6 Change of direction
6.3 Special circumstances
To turn left on interurban roads, cycles and two-wheeled mopeds must move to the right, if possible off the carriageway, and start from this position, except when there is a special lane for turning on that side.
(Página 194 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 ‘U’ turn  
7.2 Carrying out a ‘U’ turn
If the circumstances are such that an obstruction or danger would be caused to other road users by a ‘U’ turn or the continuance of a ‘U’ turn, then the manoeuvre must not be commenced or must be terminated.
(Página 194 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Maneouvres          
       
7 ‘U’ turn    
7.3 Circumstances when it is prohibited to undertake a ‘U’ turn
It is specifically prohibited to carry out a ‘U’ turn:
At level crossings (although it is not prohibited in their immediate surroundings).
In tunnels, underpasses and sections of the road affected by the signal “unnel”.
On motorways and dual carriageways, except in the places designated for this purpose.
On one-way roads and one-way sections of roads.
In general, in all sections of the road where overtaking is prohibited, unless a ‘’turn is expressly authorized.
(Página 195 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 ‘U’ turn  
7.3 Circumstances when it is prohibited to undertake a ‘U’ turn
Also, where it is not permissible to overtake (and therefore it is not possible to undertake a ‘U’ turn):
Intersections and their proximities, although the manoeuvre is permitted when there is an express priority sign on the road.
At pedestrian crossing and in the proximity of these crossings.
Carrying out a ‘U’ turn where it is not permitted (under the regulations) could result in the deduction of 3 points.
(Página 195 del manual 'Learning to drive')
